**Before Your Commute:**

*   **Morning Mobility Routine (10-15 minutes):** Since you enjoy weight training, start your day with a quick bodyweight circuit. Think squats, lunges, push-ups against a wall, and some arm circles. This will activate your muscles and get your blood flowing before you even step on the bus.
*   **Walk to the Bus Stop (5-10 minutes):** Instead of taking a tricycle or taxi the entire way, walk the first few blocks to the bus stop. This adds a little extra movement to your morning.

**During Your Bus Ride:**

*   **Seated Exercises:** While on the bus, perform subtle exercises like leg raises, ankle rotations, and shoulder rolls. These are discreet and can help prevent stiffness.
*   **Stand When Possible:** If there's space, try standing for at least part of your bus ride. This engages your core and leg muscles more than sitting.

**After Work:**

*   **Walk Part of the Way Home (15-20 minutes):** Get off the bus a few stops earlier and walk the remaining distance. This is a great way to de-stress and add some steps to your day.
*   **Post-Commute Mobility (5-10 minutes):** Before heading straight home, do a few stretches focusing on your legs and back to counteract the effects of sitting on the bus.



These suggestions aim to integrate light movement into your existing routine without feeling like a formal workout, aligning with your enjoyment of weight training and your current bus commute.
